rows.speaker: القائلون بصدور الذنب عن الأنبياء
rows.claim: Those who allow prophets to sin infer from God's reproach that the Prophet's act here was sinful.
rows.anchor: القائلون بصدور الذنب عن الأنبياء عليهم السلام تمسكوا بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the act was required in that circumstance and at most resembled leaving caution or the preferable; it was not a sin.
rows.anchor: فلم يكن ذلك ذنبا ألبتة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes agree that the one who frowned and turned away was the Messenger, and that the blind man was Ibn Umm Maktum.
rows.anchor: أجمع المفسرون على أن الذي عبس وتولى ، هو الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام ، وأجمعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A doubled reading of ʿabasa intensifies the sense, as in the doubled form kallaḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرىء عبس بالتشديد للمبالغة ونحوه كلح في / كلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative phrase an jāʾahu is governed either by the nearer tawallā or the farther ʿabasa, according to differing rules about which governor acts.
rows.anchor: أن جاءه منصوب بتولى أو بعبس على اختلاف المذهبين في إعمال الأقرب أو الأبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with two hamzas and an intervening alif pauses after ʿabasa wa-tawallā, then begins as a reproach: the blind man has now come.
rows.anchor: وقرىء أن جاءه بهمزتين ، وبألف بينهما وقف على { عبس وتولى } ثم ابتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from reporting the Prophet's lapse in the third person to addressing him directly heightens reproach, like publicly complaining and then confronting the offender.
rows.anchor: الإقبال عليه بالخطاب دليل على زيادة الإنكار

rows.speaker: القول الأول
rows.claim: The first view takes the pronoun to the blind man: what he learns may cleanse ignorance or sin, or admonish him and help him obey.
rows.anchor: الأول : أي شيء يجعلك داريا بحال هذا الأعمى لعله يتطهر بما يتلقن منك

rows.speaker: القول الثاني
rows.claim: The second view takes the pronoun to the disbeliever: perhaps he will accept Islam, or the reminder will bring him nearer to accepting truth, though you cannot know this will happen.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن الضمير في لعله للكافر ، بمعنى أنت طمعت في أن يزكى الكافر بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading fatannaʿuhu in the nominative coordinates with yadhdhakkaru; in the accusative it is a response to laʿalla, as in Ghāfir 40:37.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فتنفعه بالرفع عطفا على يذكر ، وبالنصب جوابا للعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: You are not responsible if the person you call does not accept Islam; your duty is only to convey, so zeal for their conversion must not turn you away from a believer.
rows.anchor: فإنه ليس عليك إلا البلاغ ، أي لا يبلغن بك الحرص على إسلامهم إلى أن تعرض عمن أسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasʿā means that the man hastens in seeking good, as in the command to hasten to Friday prayer, 62:9.
rows.anchor: أن يسرع في طلب الخير ، كقوله : { فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله }

rows.speaker: الوجه الأول
rows.claim: One possibility is that he fears God and fears failing to give proper attention to his religious duties.
rows.anchor: يخشى الله ويخافه في أن لا يهتم بأداء تكاليفه

rows.speaker: الوجه الثاني
rows.claim: A second possibility is that he fears the disbelievers and the harm they may cause when he comes to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أو يخشى الكفار وأذاهم في إتيانك

rows.speaker: الوجه الثالث
rows.claim: A third possibility is that, being blind and without a guide, he fears stumbling.
rows.anchor: أو يخشى الكبوة فإنه كان أعمى ، وما كان له قائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-sabīl is accusative through an elided yassiruhu, which is then supplied as its explanation.
rows.anchor: نصب السبيل بإضمار يسره ، وفسره بيسره

rows.speaker: القول الأول
rows.claim: One view is that God facilitated the infant's exit from the womb: the child turns from its initial position at birth, and surviving passage through the narrow opening is wondrous.
rows.anchor: المراد تسهيل خروجه من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim equates this with 90:10: God enables a person to choose good or evil in worldly and religious matters through capacity, instruction, reason, prophets, and revealed books.
rows.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : المراد من هذه الآية ، هو المراد من قوله : { وهديناه النجدين }

rows.speaker: القول الثالث
rows.claim: A third view restricts the facilitated path to religion, reasoning that al-sabīl suggests worldly conditions rather than matters attained in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أن هذا مخصوص بأمر الدين ، لأن لفظ السبيل مشعر بأن المقصود أحوال الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī places the facilitated path in the middle stage of human life and then identifies death, burial, and resurrection as the final stage.
rows.anchor: وأما المرتبة الثانية : وهي المرتبة الأخيرة ، فهي قوله تعالى : { ثم أماته فأقبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the preposition bi in the angels' tasbīḥ requires grammatical analysis to determine what it attaches to.
rows.anchor: وكذلك البحث عن قوله : ﴿ ونحن نسبح بحمدك ﴾ [ البقرة : 30 ] فإنه يجب البحث عن هذه الباء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An unnamed view nests all knowledge in four books, Qur'anic sciences in the Fātiḥa, and the Fātiḥa's sciences in the bāʾ of the basmala.
rows.anchor: قيل : كل العلوم مندرج في الكتب الأربعة وعلومها في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says the aim of knowledge is to bring the servant to God; the basmala's bāʾ denotes attachment and thus expresses that aim.
rows.anchor: لأن المقصود من كل العلوم وصول العبد إلى الرب وهذا الباء باء الإلصاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is declinable because its ending changes under different governing factors, as shown by min ibnika versus min al-rajuli.
rows.anchor: ههنا اختلف آخر هذه الكلمة باختلاف العوامل فإنه لا معنى للعامل إلا الأمر الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min has four uses: indicating an origin, a part, an explanation, or an augmentative function.
rows.anchor: كلمة من وردت على وجوه أربعة : ابتداء الغاية والتبعيض والتبيين والزيادة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad holds that min originally marks the beginning of an extent, with its other uses derived from that sense.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد : الأصل هو ابتداء الغاية والبواقي مفرعة عليه

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others hold that the partitive use is primary and that min's other uses derive from it.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : الأصل هو التبعيض والبواقي مفرعة عليه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians deny that min is ever augmentative; in the cited forgiveness phrase, it contributes a partitive sense, and forgiving every part amounts to forgiving all.
rows.anchor: أنكر بعضهم كونها زائدة وأما قوله تعالى : ﴿ يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī raises, without resolving here, why Satan uses min for the first two directions but ʿan for the right and left.
rows.anchor: لم خص الأولين بلفظ من والثالث والرابع بلفظ عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also asks why the formula of seeking refuge says min Satan rather than ʿan Satan.
rows.anchor: فلم جاءت الاستعاذة بلفظ من فقال { أعوذ بالله من الشيطان } ولم يقل عن الشيطان

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that seeking refuge makes the servant the originator of actions: if God creates an act, the servant cannot perform or resist it.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : قوله : ( أعوذ بالله ) يبطل القول بالجبر من وجوه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that refuge is coherent only if God did not create the evil sought refuge from; otherwise the servant seeks refuge from God's own act.
rows.anchor: أن الاستعاذة إنما تحسن من الله تعالى إذا لم يكن الله تعالى خالقا للأمور

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They infer that seeking refuge from sins shows the servant rejects them, whereas a person must accept what God decrees if God creates sins.
rows.anchor: أن الاستعاذة بالله من المعاصي تدل على أن العبد غير راض بها

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: They argue that if Satan has no role in whispering and God creates it, one should seek refuge from God rather than Satan.
rows.anchor: أما إذا كانت فعلا لله ولم يكن للشيطان في وجودها أثر البتة

words: يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: الشيطان
rows.claim: In a fifth objection, Satan says that if God decrees his whispering while affirming that He wills ease and does not burden beyond capacity, condemning him conflicts with divine wisdom and mercy.
rows.anchor: فمع هذه الأعذار الظاهرة والأسباب القوية كيف يجوز في حكمتك ورحمتك أن تذمني وتلعنني

rows.speaker: الشيطان
rows.claim: In a sixth objection, Satan asks whether his being accursed follows a sin he committed: if so determinism fails, and if not, the punishment is unjust despite God's denial of injustice.
rows.anchor: جعلتني مرجوما ملعونا بسبب جرم صدر مني أو لا بسبب جرم صدر مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects the proposed kasb as a middle position: if human power independently affects an act, the view is Muʿtazilī; if not, it is pure determinism and the objections still apply.
rows.anchor: هذا ضعيف ؛ لأنه إما أن يكون لقدرة العبد أثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says jinn and devils are not ordinary dense bodies moving about like humans and animals; he outlines two other accounts of their nature.
rows.anchor: أطبق الكل على أنه ليس الجن والشياطين عبارة عن أشخاص جسمانية كثيفة تجيء وتذهب مثل الناس والبهائم

rows.speaker: القول الأول
rows.claim: One account makes jinn and devils airy bodies that can assume different forms, reason, understand, and perform difficult tasks.
rows.anchor: الأول أنها أجسام هوائية قادرة على التشكل بأشكال مختلفة ولها عقول وأفهام

rows.speaker: كثير من الناس
rows.claim: A second account, held by many, makes them immaterial entities, neither occupying space nor inhering in bodies.
rows.anchor: أن كثيرا من الناس أثبتوا أنها موجودات غير متحيزة ولا حالة في المتحيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the immaterial account, spirits range from exalted angels to spirits managing bodies, including ranks linked to the Throne, Kursī, celestial spheres, seas, mountains, plants, and animals.
rows.anchor: ثم هذه الموجودات قد تكون عالية مقدسة عن تدبير الأجسام بالكلية وهي الملائكة المقربون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either account, benevolent, luminous spirits are called righteous jinn, while low, dark, evil spirits are called devils.
rows.anchor: قد تكون مشرقة إلهية خيرة سعيدة وهي المسماة بالصالحين من الجن

rows.speaker: المنكرون لوجود الجن والشياطين
rows.claim: The deniers argue that jinn must be either dense bodies, which healthy senses would see, or subtle bodies, which violent winds would tear and which could not perform the difficult acts attributed to them.
rows.anchor: احتج المنكرون لوجود الجن والشياطين بوجوه : الحجة الأولى

rows.speaker: المنكرون لوجود الجن والشياطين
rows.claim: They also argue that long contact with humans should create visible friendship or hostility and resulting benefits or harms, yet none is observed; even repentant conjurers deny seeing effects.
rows.anchor: إذا كانوا حاضرين في هذا العالم مخالطين للبشر فالظاهر الغالب أن يصل لهم بسبب طول المخالطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī says denying that the recited Qur'an is God's speech denies a teaching known by mass transmission from Muhammad's religion and entails unbelief.
rows.anchor: فمنكره منكر لما عرف بالتواتر من دين محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام فيلزمه الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers one argument by saying its reasoning is not peculiar to any one essence and would therefore entail that all things are eternal.
rows.anchor: ما ذكرتم غير مختص بماهية دون ماهي فيلزمكم قدم الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers another argument by calling its inference too obscure to outweigh self-evident truths.
rows.anchor: ما ذكرتم من الاستدلال خفي في مقابلة البديهيات فيكون باطلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling successive letters and sounds God's speech means, metaphorically, that the expressions signify the eternal attribute subsisting in God's essence.
rows.anchor: كان المراد أنها ألفاظ دالة على الصفة القائمة بذات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In customary oaths, the expression “God's speech” is understood according to common usage.
rows.anchor: وأما حديث الحنث والبر فذلك لأن مبنى الإيمان على العرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying God's speech is eternal refers to the eternal attribute signified by the letters and expressions.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلنا : كلام الله قديم لم نعن به إلا تلك الصفة القديمة التي هي مدلول هذه الألفاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Qur'an a miracle for Muhammad refers to created letters and sounds, since the eternal attribute existed before Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلنا : كلام الله معجزة لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عنينا به هذه الحروف وهذه الأصوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: References to Qur'anic sūras and verses mean its letters; calling it eloquent or interpreting it refers to its expressions.
rows.anchor: وإذا قلنا : كلام الله سور وآيات عنينا به هذه الحروف وإذا قلنا : كلام الله فصيح

rows.speaker: الحشوية
rows.claim: The Ḥashwiyya claim that the sounds heard from a human are themselves God's speech.
rows.anchor: زعمت الحشوية أن هذه الأصوات التي نسمعها من هذا الإنسان عين كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects this because the sounds belong to the human tongue and voice; making them God's very attribute would place one attribute in both God and a human body.
rows.anchor: هذه الحروف والأصوات التي نسمعها من هذا الإنسان صفة قائمة بلسانه وأصواته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He compares the Ḥashwiyya claim to the Christian doctrine that the divine Word dwelt in Jesus, noting that the Ḥashwiyya extend the claim to every person.
rows.anchor: ولا فرق بين القولين إلا أن النصارى قالوا بهذا القول في حق عيسى وحده

rows.speaker: مثبتو الجن والشياطين
rows.claim: Proponents of immaterial jinn describe celestial spirits as stronger causes of human spirits, guiding their human counterparts through dreams or waking inspiration.
rows.anchor: تلك الأرواح الفلكية تعين أولادها على مصالحها

rows.speaker: مثبتو الجن والشياطين
rows.claim: They say a human soul strongly connected to its celestial source can display extraordinary and supernatural acts.
rows.anchor: ظهرت عليه أفعال عجيبة وأعمال خارقة للعادات فهذا تفصيل مذاهب من يثبت الجن والشياطين

rows.speaker: قوم من الفلاسفة
rows.claim: Some philosophers object that immaterial beings cannot perceive particulars or cause particular actions.
rows.anchor: أن قوما من الفلاسفة طعنوا في هذا المذهب وزعموا أن المجرد يمتنع عليه إدراك الجزئيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that the soul judging a particular person to be human rather than a horse must perceive particulars as well as universals.
rows.anchor: يمكننا أن نحكم على هذا الشخص المعين بأنه إنسان وليس بفرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if an immaterial soul cannot initially perceive particulars, it may do so through bodily instruments, which jinn could have in the ether or frigid spheres.
rows.anchor: يمكنها أن تدرك الجزئيات بواسطة الآلات الجسمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that different kinds of bodies may share volume and magnitude yet have different natures; a subtle kind could be alive, intelligent, powerful, and self-shaping.
rows.anchor: الأجسام متساوية في الحجمية والمقدار وهذان المعنيان أعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that subtle bodies need not be torn by wind, comparing their possible penetration to lightning fire passing through stone and iron.
rows.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقال : أحد أنواع الأجسام أجسام لطيفة نفاذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this possibility, jinn could penetrate and affect human bodies and remain active until their appointed term; no proof rules out these possibilities.
rows.anchor: فكل هذه الأحوال احتمالات ظاهرة والدليل لم يقم على إبطالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the social-contact objection, al-Rāzī says friendship or enmity need not occur with everyone, and individuals do not know one another's experiences, so the matter remains possible.
rows.anchor: لا يجب حصول تلك الصداقة والعداوة مع كل واحد وكل واحد لا يعرف إلا حال نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī denies that belief in jinn and angels necessarily impugns the prophets' mission, deferring the fuller answer.
rows.anchor: لا نسلم أن القول بوجود الجن والملائكة يوجب الطعن في نبوة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ holds that seeking refuge is obligatory before every recitation, inside or outside prayer.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء : الاستعاذة واجبة لكل قراءة سواء كانت في الصلاة أو في غيرها

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sīrīn holds that one recitation of the formula during a lifetime suffices to discharge the obligation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين : إذا تعوذ الرجل مرة واحدة في عمره فقد كفى في إسقاط الوجوب

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining jurists hold that seeking refuge is not obligatory.
rows.anchor: وقال الباقون : إنها غير واجبة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority cite the Prophet's failure to teach the formula among a Bedouin's prayer practices; an objection says that report does not enumerate every prayer obligation, so its silence proves little.
rows.anchor: حجة الجمهور أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يعلم الأعرابي الاستعاذة

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ argues that the Prophet maintained the practice and that believers are commanded to follow him, supporting its obligation.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام واظب عليه فيكون واجبا لقوله تعالى : ﴿ واتبعوه ﴾

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He argues that the imperative to seek refuge is obligatory at every recitation, since the ruling recurs whenever its stated cause, reciting Qur'an, recurs.
rows.anchor: احتج عطاء على وجوب الاستعاذة بوجوه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He argues that repelling Satan's harm is obligatory, and whatever is necessary to fulfill an obligation is itself obligatory.
rows.anchor: ودفع شر الشيطان واجب وما لا يتم الواجب إلا به فهو واجب

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He also cites precaution as a reason to perform the formula.
rows.anchor: طريقة الاحتياط توجب الاستعاذة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most jurists consider seeking refuge recommended before recitation; Mālik omits it in obligatory prayers but uses it in Ramadan night prayer.
rows.anchor: التعوذ مستحب قبل القراءة عند الأكثرين وقال مالك لا يتعوذ في المكتوبة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī reports that Ibn ʿUmar recited the formula quietly and Abū Hurayra aloud, and permits either, though his al-Imlāʾ prefers loud recitation.
rows.anchor: روي أن عبد الله بن عمر لما قرأ أسر بالتعوذ وعن أبي هريرة أنه جهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī reasons that the formula resembles the opening supplication more than al-Fātiḥa, favoring quiet recitation; loudness is a positive quality while quiet is its absence.
rows.anchor: المشابهة بينها وبين الافتتاح أتم لكون كل واحد منهما نافلة عند الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names of the vowel marks derive from articulation: ḍamma closes and raises the lips, fatḥa opens the mouth, and kasra lowers the jaw; jazm means cutting, while the senses of waqf and sukūn are evident.
rows.anchor: وأما الجزم فهو القطع وأما أنه لم سمي وقفا وسكونا فعلته ظاهرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some grammarians reserve fatḥa, ḍamma, kasra, and waqf for built forms, while the other four terms name inflectional states.
rows.anchor: منهم من زعم أن الفتح والضم والكسر والوقف أسماء للأحوال البنائية

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others use the first four names for both built and inflected states, treating the second four as narrower names for inflection; the first set is thus genus to the second.
rows.anchor: وجعل الأربعة الثانية أسماء للأحوال الإعرابية فتكون الأربعة الأولى بالنسبة إلى الأربعة الثانية كالجنس

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh calls the vocalic states al-majārī and counts eight.
rows.anchor: أن سيبويه يسميها بالمجاري ويقول : هي ثمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī explains the name al-majārī by saying the so-called movement is a voiced sound produced as breath flows and extends after a consonant.
rows.anchor: فهذا الحرف المصوت إنما حدث لجريان نفسه وامتداده

rows.speaker: المازني
rows.claim: Al-Māzinī says Sībawayh errs by calling the states of built words al-majārī, since only changing inflectional states should count as things that flow.
rows.anchor: قال المازني : غلط سيبويه في تسميته الحركات البنائية بالمجاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that built forms change between connected speech and pause, so their states are not wholly fixed and can still be called al-majārī.
rows.anchor: المبنيات قد تحرك عند الدرج ولا تحرك عند الوقف فلم تكن تلك الأحوال لازمة لها مطلقا
